issues: No integrity problems found. The candidate only uses train_smiles and train_y. Model selection happens inside fit_predict on an internal split of the training fold. There is no file or network access, nothing is hard-coded and no test labels are used.

Weakness, not a bug: the internal 80/20 split is random rather than grouped by Murcko scaffold. Molecules with the same scaffold can land on both sides, so the validation score is optimistic. It tends to pick max_features values that suit memorising known scaffolds rather than predicting new ones. Using only one 20% split also makes the choice noisy. Both points help explain why the candidate is worse.
Runtime is fine: about 6 random-forest fits per fold, roughly 6 times the 16 s baseline, which stays well under the 10-minute limit.

The extra code adds complexity and makes the score worse, so it should not be kept.
